body:
PR #2000 for BUG-1287 — the investigation-first acceptance paid off, and it found genuine unshipped work that a blanket fix would have deleted

Open on bug-1287. No verdict from me, I wrote the prompt.

THE CLASSIFICATION ANSWERS YOUR QUESTION. Seventeen held leases, each classified by which predicate failed:

  process still running          1   correct, deferred to the notify path
  spec not finished              4   correct — verified genuinely In Progress / Approved / NeedsAttention
  no merge signal                4   correct — verified genuinely OPEN PRs via the forge
  "merged, but N unmerged"       7   MIXED, and this is the interesting bucket

So: NOT a BUG-1286 symptom. You asked for that to be established before any code, and it was — the four "spec not finished" cases are genuinely unfinished rather than specs whose completion event never fired. Predicate 2, the ancestry test, is at fault on its own.

THE PART THAT JUSTIFIES THE SEQUENCING YOU INSISTED ON. Of those 7, it verified each by patch-id against the actual squash commit rather than assuming the prior:

  BUG-1163, BUG-1167, BUG-1268, STORY-1129   1 commit each, patch-id byte-identical to what landed. Pure artifact.
  TASK-1251                                   2 commits, main's squash combined both. Pure artifact.
  BUG-1177                                    4 commits — 1 landed, THREE ARE GENUINE UNSHIPPED WORK. Correctly kept.
  TASK-1285                                   10 commits, likely genuine active work. Left alone.

A blanket "squash-merge means ancestry lies, therefore reap" would have destroyed three real commits on BUG-1177 and possibly ten on TASK-1285. Your acceptance criterion — classify before changing the reaper — is the only reason that did not happen, and it is worth noting that the strong prior we both held was right about five cases out of seven and wrong about the two that mattered.

I VERIFIED THE SAFETY GATE MYSELF rather than taking it from the report, since this is the one change where being wrong deletes work:

  let content_fully_landed = if pr_merged && unique_unmerged_commits > 0 {

It cannot fire on an unmerged branch. The dirty, locked, live-process and protected-branch gates are untouched, and stale remote branches are still only reported, never deleted — as you required.

Reported, not re-run by me: 5121 tests pass, fmt clean. Tests include a real-git-repo fixture distinguishing shipped from unshipped squash branches, and a reap fixture with one reapable and one not-yet-reapable case.

TWO THINGS THIS FEEDS.

BUG-1307, the stranded-branch spec, now has confirmed content rather than a hypothesis: BUG-1177 carries three genuinely unshipped commits and TASK-1285 ten, neither with a PR, neither reported by any surface. That is the population that spec is about, and it is now evidenced rather than inferred.

And 141 GiB does not get reclaimed by this. Five worktrees become reapable; the two with real work stay, correctly. I would rather say that plainly than let the disk number imply a bigger win than there is.

The other lane, BUG-1289, is still running.
